facility_roles.quote: A short-baseline experiment in the CERN SPS Wide Band Neutrino Beam [3] was well suited for this search.

intervals.label: first operation (CERN Courier: began operation in 1993)
intervals.note: The Courier says the detector began operation in 1993; the collaboration's own paper dates its data taking from 1994. The 1993-1994 period is recorded as commissioning/first operation, an interpretation that no source spells out.
intervals.quote: With the West Area well served with muon neutrinos, specialized detectors (NOMAD using kinematic techniques, and CHORUS using nuclear emulsion to observe the final state tau leptons) began operation in 1993.

intervals.label: data taking
intervals.note: Year precision, from the final-results paper. A conference summary (hep-ex/0206006) gives 'the years 1994-1998' for CHORUS and NOMAD together and the CERN Courier says the West Area neutrino experiments finished in September 1998; the data of the final analysis are those of 1994-1997.
intervals.quote: The CHORUS experiment took data from 1994 to 1997.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event: end of data taking at year precision. The CERN Courier (27 November 1998) dates the completion of the CHORUS and NOMAD experiments to September 1998; not used because the CHORUS data set ends in 1997.
intervals.quote: The CHORUS experiment took data from 1994 to 1997.

The average neutrino energy is 26 GeV, well above the τ production threshold.

lineage.quote: Another experiment, NOMAD, used the same beam and searched for ντ appearance using a purely electronic technique [4].

name: CHORUS
notes: No official CHORUS website survives (the experiment ended in the 1990s); no website is recorded.

The experiment's data-taking years conflict between sources (1994-1997 in the final paper; 1994-1998 in a conference summary; operation from 1993 and completion in September 1998 in the CERN Courier). See the intervals' notes.

physics_goals.quote: The CHORUS experiment was designed to search for νµ → ντ oscillations through the observation of charged-current interactions ντ N → τ − X followed by the decay of the τ lepton, directly observed in a nuclear emulsion target.
physics_goals.value: Search for muon-neutrino to tau-neutrino oscillation by observing tau-neutrino charged-current interactions and the decay of the tau lepton directly in a nuclear emulsion target

summary.plain: A hybrid detector at CERN that hunted for muon neutrinos turning into tau neutrinos, by looking for the short kink of a tau lepton in a 770 kg block of nuclear emulsion. It ran in 1994-97, saw no signal, and set a tight limit on the mixing.
summary.technical: Hybrid emulsion/electronic experiment in the CERN SPS wide-band nu_mu beam (mean energy 26 GeV): 770 kg nuclear-emulsion target in four stacks, scintillating-fibre target tracker, air-core hadron spectrometer, calorimeters and a magnetised-iron muon spectrometer. Searched for nu_tau charged-current interactions via the tau decay seen in emulsion. Final analysis of the 1994-1997 data: sin^2(2 theta_mu_tau) < 4.4e-4 (90 % CL) at large delta m^2.
